findings.passage: Here, in Georgia, you can carry a gun almost anywhere – onto a college campus, at a public concert, at a nightclub, into a school.
findings.note: Campaign-site post written while she was a candidate; criticises how widely guns may be carried in Georgia and says she rallied with a gun-safety group for common sense gun laws.
subjects: carry a gun in public places

findings.passage: Last week, I rallied with Moms Demand Action at the Gold Dome (video). Few Republican legislators would listen to our calls for common sense gun laws.
findings.note: Says she took part in a gun-safety rally at the Capitol and calls for common sense gun laws.

findings.passage: This week, I filed my legislation, SB50, repealing the “Campus Carry” law that allows licensed gun owners to bring guns onto Georgia’s public college campuses.
findings.note: Her own post announcing that she filed SB 50 (2019) to repeal Georgia's campus carry law.

findings.passage: Campus Carry was never about making our college campuses safer.
findings.note: Her stated reason for repealing campus carry; the same post also argues that assault-style weapons are used in mass murders and that gun reform has been blocked by gun lobbyists.

findings.passage: The NRA loses money and power if people start to agree that military assault-style weapons are more likely to be used to commit mass murder than they are to protect a citizen from government encroachment.
findings.note: Her description of the gun lobby's interest, in a post about repealing campus carry.

findings.passage: This week, we debated SB 344, a 5-day tax holiday for gun sales.
findings.note: Her newsletter (page stamped 2024-02-11) on the Senate floor debate over SB 344, the gun-sale tax holiday bill; she then reports that another senator argued other goods deserve a tax holiday.

findings.passage: SB 204 expands Georgia’s firearms preemption law by prohibiting local governments from regulating gun storage — directly targeting ordinances like Savannah’s, which made it a crime to leave a firearm in an unlocked vehicle.
findings.note: Her newsletter describing SB 204 (state preemption of local gun-storage rules) which passed the Senate on party lines; she headlines the item as gun policy that abolishes local control.
subjects: state preemption of local gun laws

findings.note: Named in the news report as one of the senators co-signing Senate Resolution 605, which reaffirms Georgians' right under the Second Amendment to own and carry a firearm and condemns a shooting by federal agents. Co-sponsorship; source is a news report, not the legislature's page.
